title: Deviating from industry norms is encouraged for security, while deviating from Sky's own patterns is not
content:
A.1.10.2.4.7.4.6 contains an inversion worth reading twice. On internal precedent it is strict: "All existing Sky processes and patterns, whether pertaining to rules, processes, systems, smart contracts, or code, must be complied with." Deviation is permitted only where "regular operation is impossible due to a technical limitation or otherwise," and even then "new patterns developed in this way must prioritize the safety and security of the Sky Protocol over all other considerations and should be **as similar to old patterns as possible**."

On external precedent it is permissive: "However, deviation from industry norms and best practices is **encouraged** so long as they are made in the interest of maximizing security."

Most engineering cultures rank these the other way — industry best practice is the authority, local convention the thing to be modernized. The reversal follows from the Lindy principle at A.1.10.2.4.7.4.4. A Sky pattern's authority comes from having survived in this specific adversarial environment with this specific money at stake; an industry norm's authority comes from popularity, which is evidence about the average system rather than about Sky's.

The "as similar to old patterns as possible" clause is the operative constraint when deviation is unavoidable: minimize the *distance* travelled, because the value of a precedent decays with how far the new thing sits from it. Reviewers can then diff against something familiar instead of evaluating a novel construction from first principles.

The accountability hook is the closing sentence — "any deviations by the Crafter or Reviewers must be communicated to the Core Facilitator" — so departures from precedent are surfaced rather than absorbed silently into the next Spell's baseline.
description: A.1.10.2.4.7.4.6 inverts the usual hierarchy: internal precedent outranks external best practice, and any unavoidable new pattern must stay as close to the old one as possible.
